post_title: What percentage of respiratory specimens tested for influenza in U.S. clinical laboratories will be positive in CDC's FluView report for Week 44 (week ending November 7, 2026)?

question.title: What percentage of respiratory specimens tested for influenza in U.S. clinical laboratories will be positive in CDC's FluView report for Week 44 (week ending November 7, 2026)?
question.description:
CDC's FluView is the agency's weekly U.S. influenza surveillance report, published on Fridays after 11:00 a.m. ET, with each edition covering the MMWR week that ended on the preceding Saturday. Its headline virologic indicator is the national percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for influenza in clinical laboratories (NREVSS network) — a leading indicator of influenza virus circulation that CDC uses, alongside outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) data, to say whether activity is increasing or decreasing.

The 2026–27 season has started unusually early and fast. National clinical-laboratory percent positive has climbed from 2.7% in Week 37 (week ending Sept. 19, 2026) to 3.9% (Week 39), 5.0% (Week 40), 5.7% (Week 41, week ending Oct. 17) and 7.6% in the most recent edition, Week 42 (week ending Oct. 24, 2026). CDC reported that the Week 41 influenza hospitalization rate was the highest for that week since 2010–11, that 98.9% of subtyped influenza A viruses in Week 42 were A(H1N1)pdm09, that 2.4% of outpatient visits were for ILI, that about 6,100 people were admitted to hospital with influenza in Week 42, that one influenza-associated pediatric death had been reported for the season, and that the cumulative influenza hospitalization rate stood at 3.9 per 100,000.

For context on how fast this indicator can move in early November: in the early 2022–23 wave, percent positive reached double digits by mid-November, whereas in several other recent seasons it was still in the mid-single digits at that point in the calendar. Week-to-week changes in the fall typically range from roughly flat to +2 percentage points, and the indicator is noisy because specimen volume and the mix of reporting sites shift from week to week. Seasonal influenza percent positive normally keeps climbing from November into December or January, but local plateaus and temporary dips are common.

The edition that resolves this question is the one for Week 44 (November 1–7, 2026), due Friday, November 13, 2026. Forecasting opens around November 12, 2026, by which point the latest available edition is expected to be Week 43 (week ending Oct. 31, 2026, published Nov. 6, 2026) — so this requires a one-week-ahead forecast of a rapidly changing, noisy indicator, informed by regional patterns in recent editions, ILI and hospitalization trends, subtype composition, and how comparable early-season waves have behaved. FluView data are explicitly preliminary and subject to revision; the question resolves on the figure printed in the Week 44 edition itself, not on later revised figures.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the national percentage of respiratory specimens testing positive for influenza virus in clinical laboratories reported for Week 44 in CDC's FluView. The source is the Week 44 edition (week ending November 7, 2026), expected at https://www.cdc.gov/fluview/surveillance/2026-week-44.html (also reachable at https://www.cdc.gov/fluview/surveillance/index.html?wk=44); the figure to use is the percentage shown in the "No. of positive specimens (%)" row of that edition's clinical-laboratories table for Week 44. If that national percent-positive cell is absent or unreadable in the Week 44 table, the national percent-positive figure stated in that same edition's narrative text is used instead. For scale, the Week 42 edition states the figure as "7.6% positive for influenza in clinical labs", so a Week 44 figure of 12.4% would resolve as 12.4. Figures appearing in later FluView editions (revisions) do not affect resolution; if the Week 44 edition is published later than November 13, 2026, resolution waits for its publication, and if no Week 44 edition has been published by December 11, 2026, the Week 44 national percent-positive value shown in CDC's FluView Interactive dashboard (https://gis.cdc.gov/grasp/fluview/fluportaldashboard.html) is used.
question.fine_print: "Week 44" refers to CDC's MMWR week 44 of 2026, the week of November 1–7, 2026 (Saturday, November 7, 2026, is the week-ending date).
